jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, PKI & Cryptographic Systems

reading.body:
Four cryptography job postings, three at ServiceNow and one at Cloudflare, are the entire sample behind this view of AI hiring in the field.

The pattern is concentration. ServiceNow accounts for three of the four roles, two of them identical senior platform cryptography positions split between Santa Clara and San Diego, and the third a staff-level version of the same title. Cloudflare contributes one senior PKI and cryptographic systems role. Every posting is a senior or staff engineering position, none is junior, and all four sit in the security category.

Cryptography is the layer that makes compute trustworthy at scale. Training clusters, inference endpoints, and the keys and certificates that authenticate them all depend on this work, so hiring here is a precondition for AI infrastructure rather than a product of it. The locations matter too: Santa Clara and San Diego are established hardware and cloud corridors, which is consistent with cryptography roles clustering where the machines and the operators already are.

What this does not tell you is the size of the market. Four postings from two companies over roughly a week is a snapshot, not a trend, and the source list includes aggregators and federal boards that contributed nothing to this set. Nothing here shows whether cryptography hiring is rising or falling, what these roles pay, or how they compare with demand for the compute and power they protect.
